mainTopic: Prayer while traveling, the direction of prayer, and the opening of the משנה on מוסף
overview: The גמרא finishes its discussion of the traveler's prayer: its plural wording, when to say it, the length of journey that calls for it, and whether one must stand for it. It then compares הֲבִינֵנוּ with תְּפִלָּה קְצָרָה and rules that only הֲבִינֵנוּ counts as a completed prayer and must be said standing. A ברייתא about praying while riding a donkey follows, and the הלכה is set like רבי: the rider stays seated. Another ברייתא teaches that every person directs his heart, step by step, toward the קֹדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים, so that all יִשְׂרָאֵל pray toward one place. The גמרא then looks at sages who arranged their prayer around travel or a festival lecture, and at the dispute over whether standing or joining גְּאוּלָּה to תְּפִלָּה comes first. A new משנה begins on whether מוסף is only for a חבר עיר. The גמרא shows how רבי יהודה's version differs from the first version and rules like רבי יהודה. שמואל's supporting statement continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Include everyone in the request
steps.stepSummary: A traveler should pray in language that includes the community.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person should join himself with the community.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a rule for the wording of the traveler’s prayer. The person praying should speak as part of a group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The instruction concerns whom the request includes. The next step will show what that sounds like in the prayer itself.

phrases.english: A person should join himself with the community.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This amud opens with an instruction about the prayer’s wording.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The traveler includes the community when asking for a safe journey.

steps.title: Use plural words in the prayer
steps.stepSummary: The example says “our God” and “lead us,” rather than asking only for oneself.
steps.simpleTranslation: How should one say it? “May it be Your will, Lord our God, that You lead us to peace,” and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how to put that instruction into words and gives the opening of the prayer. It is showing the plural wording to use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: “Our” and “us” make the earlier rule concrete. The quotation gives an example of the wording, not a new rule about when to pray.

phrases.english: How should one say it? “May it be Your will
Lord our God, that You lead us to peace,” and so on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the wording requested by the preceding instruction.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Say the prayer in the plural, including “our God” and “lead us.”

steps.title: Begin once the journey has begun
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב reports רב חסדא’s answer about when to say the traveler’s prayer.
steps.simpleTranslation: When does one pray? רבי יעקב said in the name of רב חסדא: From the time one is traveling on the road.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns from wording to timing. It answers that the prayer begins after the traveler has started along the road.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer identifies the start of the journey as the starting point. It does not yet address how long the journey must be.

phrases.english: When does one pray? Rabbi Ya'akov said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: מִשָּׁעָה שֶׁמְּהַלֵּךְ בַּדֶּרֶךְ.
phrases.english: in the name of Rav Ḥisda: From when one is traveling on the road.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the prayer’s wording to its timing.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One prays from the time one is traveling on the road.

steps.title: A journey of at least one פַּרְסָה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a distance threshold for the traveler’s prayer.
steps.simpleTranslation: How far? רבי יעקב said in the name of רב חסדא: Up to a פַּרְסָה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about the journey’s distance. It gives a פַּרְסָה as the measure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here “how far” is understood as asking what length of journey calls for the prayer. Following בה״ג, the answer means a journey of at least a פַּרְסָה. רש״י instead reads it as a time limit: one may say the prayer only until one has traveled a פַּרְסָה.

keyTerms.meaning: the sage whose ruling is being reported

phrases.english: How far? Rabbi Ya'akov said
in the name of Rav Ḥisda: Up to a parasang.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a distance measure after the timing rule.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A פַּרְסָה is the stated measure for the journey.

steps.title: Standing or walking while praying
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא requires standing; רב ששת allows praying even while walking.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does one pray it? רב חסדא says: Standing. רב ששת says: Even while walking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks about the traveler’s position during the prayer. It presents two views rather than resolving them here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא says to stand. רב ששת’s “even” permits walking; it does not say that walking is better than standing.

keyTerms.meaning: the sage who permits praying while walking

phrases.english: And how does one pray it?
Rav Ḥisda says: Standing.
Rav Sheshet says: Even while walking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from when to pray to whether one must stop walking.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב חסדא requires standing; רב ששת permits praying while walking.

steps.title: רב חסדא stands on the road
steps.stepSummary: While traveling together, רב חסדא stands to pray, and רב ששת asks what he is doing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא and רב ששת were walking on the road. רב חסדא stood and prayed. רב ששת asked his attendant what רב חסדא was doing, and the attendant answered that he was standing and praying.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a road-side incident involving the two sages whose views were just stated. This sets up רב ששת’s response in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא acts in line with his requirement to stand. רב ששת learns of that action through his attendant; his own choice has not yet been reported.

phrases.aramaic: רַב חִסְדָּא וְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת הֲווֹ קָאָזְלִי בְּאוֹרְחָא,
phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda and Rav Sheshet were walking on the road,
and Rav Ḥisda stood and prayed.
Rav Sheshet said to his attendant:
What is Rav Ḥisda doing?
He told him: He is standing and praying.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִסְדָּא וְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת הֲווֹ קָאָזְלִי בְּאוֹרְחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins an incident involving the two positions just presented.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The incident shows רב חסדא standing to pray; רב ששת’s reaction follows.

steps.title: רב ששת chooses to stand too
steps.stepSummary: Although רב ששת permits walking, he asks to stand and pray in this situation.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Stand me up too, and I will pray. “From being good, do not be called bad.”
steps.whatsHappening: The incident ends with רב ששת asking to stand as well. He gives a short saying to explain why he chooses the more careful option.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His earlier view allowed prayer while walking; it did not require walking. Since standing is available here, he chooses it without withdrawing his permission to pray while walking.

keyTerms.meaning: do not avoid doing better when you can

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לֵיהּ: אוֹקְמַן נָמֵי לְדִידִי וַאֲצַלֵּי,
phrases.english: He said to him: Stand me up too, and I will pray,
“From being good, do not be called bad.”

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לֵיהּ: אוֹקְמַן נָמֵי לְדִידִי וַאֲצַלֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the incident by reporting רב ששת’s response.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב ששת’s permission to pray while walking is compatible with choosing to stand when convenient.

steps.title: How do the two shortened prayers differ?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the practical difference between הֲבִינֵנוּ and תְּפִלָּה קְצָרָה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between הֲבִינֵנוּ and תְּפִלָּה קְצָרָה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the traveler’s prayer and opens a comparison of two shortened prayers. It asks what changes in practice between them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both prayers are shorter than the full prayer, so length alone does not explain the distinction. The following steps compare what must be said with each one and whether one must pray again at home.

keyTerms.meaning: the abridged prayer called “Grant us understanding”

phrases.english: What difference is there between “Grant us understanding” and a brief prayer?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new comparison after the road-side incident.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which requirements and later obligations differ between הֲבִינֵנוּ and תְּפִלָּה קְצָרָה?

steps.title: הֲבִינֵנוּ completes the prayer
steps.stepSummary: הֲבִינֵנוּ includes the first and last three blessings, and no repeat prayer is needed at home.
steps.simpleTranslation: For הֲבִינֵנוּ, one must pray the first three and the last three blessings; upon reaching home, one need not pray again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the first half of its answer, describing what accompanies הֲבִינֵנוּ. It also says what happens after the person gets home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first and last three blessings remain in place around the shortened middle. Because this prayer fulfills the obligation, reaching home does not create a need to repeat it.

phrases.english: For “Grant us understanding,” one must pray the first three
and the last three,
and when one reaches home,
one need not return to pray again,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the comparison first for הֲבִינֵנוּ.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: הֲבִינֵנוּ retains the opening and closing three blessings and does not require repetition at home.

steps.title: The brief prayer must be followed by prayer at home
steps.stepSummary: תְּפִלָּה קְצָרָה has neither set of three blessings, and the person must pray again upon reaching home.
steps.simpleTranslation: With תְּפִלָּה קְצָרָה, one need not pray either the first three or the last three blessings; when one reaches home, one must return to pray.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the other half of the comparison. It explains that the brief prayer is said without those blessings but does not finish the obligation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike הֲבִינֵנוּ, this prayer has neither the opening nor the closing three blessings. Its immediate use does not remove the need to pray when the person gets home.
steps.whatToRemember: הֲבִינֵנוּ includes the first and last three blessings and needs no repeat. תְּפִלָּה קְצָרָה omits them and must be followed by prayer at home.

phrases.english: With the brief prayer, one need not pray

phrases.aramaic: לָא שָׁלֹשׁ קַמָּיָיתָא וְלָא שָׁלֹשׁ בָּתְרָיָיתָא,
phrases.english: neither the first three nor the last three,
and when one reaches home,
one must return to pray.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the comparison by stating the rules for תְּפִלָּה קְצָרָה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: הֲבִינֵנוּ counts as the completed prayer; תְּפִלָּה קְצָרָה does not, so prayer is required again at home.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: תְּפִלָּה קְצָרָה omits the first and last three blessings and requires praying again at home.

steps.title: Which travel prayer requires standing
steps.stepSummary: הֲבִינֵנוּ requires standing; תְּפִלָּה קְצָרָה may be said while standing or walking.
steps.simpleTranslation: The practical ruling is: Say הֲבִינֵנוּ while standing. Say תְּפִלָּה קְצָרָה either while standing or while walking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the practical ruling after distinguishing these two prayers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier discussion distinguished what each prayer contains. This line adds a difference in how each one is said.

keyTerms.meaning: the shortened form of the weekday prayer
a brief prayer for a difficult situation

steps.whatToRemember: הֲבִינֵנוּ requires standing; תְּפִלָּה קְצָרָה does not.

phrases.english: And the practical ruling is: ‘Grant us understanding’ is said standing,

phrases.aramaic: תְּפִלָּה קְצָרָה, בֵּין מְעוּמָּד בֵּין מְהַלֵּךְ.
phrases.english: a brief prayer may be said whether standing or walking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the practical standing rule to the distinction completed in step 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Stand for הֲבִינֵנוּ; one may stand or walk for תְּפִלָּה קְצָרָה.

steps.title: The first rule for praying while riding
steps.stepSummary: A teaching says that a rider should dismount to pray if someone can hold the donkey; otherwise, the rider prays in place.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא turns to someone riding a donkey. The חכמים teach: If prayer time arrives and someone can hold the donkey, the rider should get down and pray. If no one can, the rider should stay where they are and pray.
steps.whatsHappening: The opening words point back to the earlier case of a rider. The גמרא then brings a teaching that sets up the rule and the disagreement that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This first view makes dismounting depend on whether someone can hold the donkey. Without that help, the rider remains seated and prays.

phrases.english: One who was riding on a donkey, etc.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָיָה רוֹכֵב עַל הַחֲמוֹר
phrases.english: The Sages taught: One who was riding on a donkey
and the time for prayer arrived,

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ לוֹ מִי שֶׁיֹּאחַז אֶת חֲמוֹרוֹ —
phrases.english: if there is someone to hold his donkey—
he should get down and pray,
but if not, he should stay in his place and pray.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיָה רוֹכֵב עַל הַחֲמוֹר וְכוּ׳. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from prayers said while traveling to the case of praying while riding.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first view requires the rider to dismount when someone can hold the donkey.

steps.title: רבי says the rider should remain seated
steps.stepSummary: רבי says the rider should pray in place even when someone could hold the donkey, because the rider will not be settled in mind.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: In either case, the rider should stay in place and pray, because the rider’s mind will not be settled.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי gives a different rule for the same rider. He says the rider stays seated whether or not someone can hold the donkey.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view treated help with the donkey as the deciding factor. רבי instead points to the rider’s state of mind when praying.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ
phrases.english: Rabbi says: In either case,
he should stay in his place and pray,
because his mind will not be settled.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first rule about dismounting when help is available.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי says to remain seated and pray in either case.

steps.title: The ruling follows רבי
steps.stepSummary: רבא, or according to another attribution רבי יהושע בן לוי, rules like רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said—and some say it was רבי יהושע בן לוי—that the law follows רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now states which side of the disagreement to follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling adopts רבי’s instruction to remain seated and pray. The text gives two possible attributions for who stated that ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: the אמורא named first as giving the ruling
the אמורא named as the alternative source of the ruling

steps.whatToRemember: For the rider in this case, the ruling follows רבי: remain seated and pray.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי:
phrases.english: Rava said, and some say Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
The law follows Rabbi.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the disagreement in favor of רבי.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The practical ruling for the rider follows רבי.

steps.title: Where to direct the heart when direction is unclear
steps.stepSummary: A blind person or someone unable to determine directions should direct the heart toward the Father in Heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: A blind person, or someone who cannot determine the directions, should direct the heart toward אָבִיו שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם, as it says: ‘And they shall pray to the Lord.’
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new case: someone who cannot tell which way to face for prayer. It gives that person an instruction and cites a verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem here is finding a direction, not deciding whether to dismount. The teaching tells the person to focus the heart toward God; the quoted verse speaks of praying to God.

keyTerms.meaning: and they shall pray to the Lord

steps.whyThisMatters: Being unable to determine a direction does not prevent a person from praying.

phrases.english: The Sages taught: A blind person

phrases.aramaic: וּמִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לְכַוֵּין אֶת הָרוּחוֹת —
phrases.english: or someone who cannot determine the directions—
should direct his heart toward his Father in Heaven,
as it is stated: ‘And they shall pray to the Lord.’

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: סוֹמֵא וּמִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לְכַוֵּין אֶת הָרוּחוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the rider’s case and opens a case about someone unable to determine the direction for prayer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone unable to determine the directions should direct the heart toward אָבִיו שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם.

steps.title: Direct the heart toward the land and then the city
steps.stepSummary: Someone outside אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל directs the heart toward it; someone within it directs the heart toward יְרוּשָׁלַיִם.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a person is outside אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל, they direct their heart toward it. If they are in אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל, they direct their heart toward יְרוּשָׁלַיִם. A verse is given for each instruction.
steps.whatsHappening: The teaching now gives a direction for a person who knows where they are. It begins with two broad locations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The target changes with the person's starting point: from outside the land, toward the land; from within the land, toward the city. Each direction is linked to wording from a verse.

phrases.english: If he was standing outside the land—

phrases.aramaic: יְכַוֵּין אֶת לִבּוֹ כְּנֶגֶד אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: he should direct his heart toward the Land of Israel,
as it says: “And they shall pray to You by way of their land.”
If he was standing in the Land of Israel—
he should direct his heart toward Jerusalem,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְהִתְפַּלְלוּ אֶל ה׳ דֶּרֶךְ הָעִיר אֲשֶׁר בָּחַרְתָּ״.
phrases.english: as it says: “And they shall pray to the Lord by way of the city that You chose.”

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The previous teaching addressed someone who cannot determine a direction; this one begins giving directions to someone who can.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Direct the heart toward אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל from outside it, and toward יְרוּשָׁלַיִם from within it.

steps.title: Move the focus inward from the city to the Temple
steps.stepSummary: A person in יְרוּשָׁלַיִם directs the heart toward בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ; a person there directs it toward בֵּית קׇדְשֵׁי הַקֳּדָשִׁים.
steps.simpleTranslation: In יְרוּשָׁלַיִם, direct the heart toward בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ. In בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ, direct it toward בֵּית קׇדְשֵׁי הַקֳּדָשִׁים. Each instruction has a supporting verse.
steps.whatsHappening: The teaching continues the same pattern, moving inward from the city to the building and then to its innermost space.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being closer does not end the instruction to direct the heart. Each new starting place has a more specific target.

keyTerms.meaning: this house, in the quoted verse

phrases.english: If he was standing in Jerusalem—

phrases.aramaic: יְכַוֵּין אֶת לִבּוֹ כְּנֶגֶד בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ,
phrases.english: he should direct his heart toward the Temple,
as it says: “And they shall pray toward this house.”
If he was standing in the Temple—

phrases.aramaic: יְכַוֵּין אֶת לִבּוֹ כְּנֶגֶד בֵּית קׇדְשֵׁי הַקֳּדָשִׁים,
phrases.english: he should direct his heart toward the Holy of Holies,
as it says: “And they shall pray toward this place.”

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It continues the sequence of increasingly specific destinations for the heart.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Within יְרוּשָׁלַיִם, direct the heart toward בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ; within בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ, toward בֵּית קׇדְשֵׁי הַקֳּדָשִׁים.

steps.title: Keep the focus on the ark-cover even from behind it
steps.stepSummary: The innermost target is בֵּית הַכַּפּוֹרֶת; someone behind it pictures themselves as standing before it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone is in בֵּית קׇדְשֵׁי הַקֳּדָשִׁים, they direct their heart toward בֵּית הַכַּפּוֹרֶת. If they stand behind בֵּית הַכַּפּוֹרֶת, they picture themselves as if they were before it.
steps.whatsHappening: The teaching reaches its most specific point, then explains what to do if someone stands behind it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The target remains הַכַּפּוֹרֶת even when a person's position makes “toward it” less obvious. The instruction to picture oneself before it keeps the same focus.

phrases.english: If he was standing in the Holy of Holies—

phrases.aramaic: יְכַוֵּין אֶת לִבּוֹ כְּנֶגֶד בֵּית הַכַּפּוֹרֶת.
phrases.english: he should direct his heart toward the place of the ark-cover.
If he was standing behind the place of the ark-cover—
he should picture himself as if he were before the ark-cover.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It takes the inward sequence to its final target and handles a difficult position relative to that target.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Direct the heart toward בֵּית הַכַּפּוֹרֶת; from behind it, picture oneself as before it.

steps.title: All directions lead to one place
steps.stepSummary: The teaching spells out which way to face from each side and concludes that all יִשְׂרָאֵל direct their hearts to one place.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the east, face west; in the west, face east; in the south, face north; and in the north, face south. Thus all יִשְׂרָאֵל direct their hearts toward one place.
steps.whatsHappening: The teaching now draws out the practical pattern behind the location-by-location instructions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People do not all face the same compass direction. They face toward the same destination from different starting points.
steps.whatToRemember: The compass direction depends on where the person stands; the place they direct their heart toward is shared.

phrases.aramaic: נִמְצָא עוֹמֵד בַּמִּזְרָח מַחֲזִיר פָּנָיו לַמַּעֲרָב.
phrases.english: It follows that one standing in the east turns his face west.
In the west, he turns his face east.
In the south, he turns his face north.
In the north, he turns his face south.

phrases.aramaic: נִמְצְאוּ כׇּל יִשְׂרָאֵל מְכַוְּונִין אֶת לִבָּם לְמָקוֹם אֶחָד.
phrases.english: Thus all Israel direct their hearts toward one place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It sums up the full sequence by showing how people in different locations share one focus.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Different starting points require different facing directions, but all direct the heart toward one place.

steps.title: A verse hints at the shared destination
steps.stepSummary: רַבִּי אָבִין, or רַבִּי אֲבִינָא, reads תַּלְפִּיּוֹת as a hill toward which all mouths turn.
steps.simpleTranslation: רַבִּי אָבִין—or, according to another attribution, רַבִּי אֲבִינָא—asks which verse points to this idea. He cites “Your neck is like the tower of David, built with turrets,” and explains it as a hill toward which all mouths turn.
steps.whatsHappening: After stating the shared destination, the גמרא adds a verse that hints at it through a wordplay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word תַּלְפִּיּוֹת is read as תֵּל together with פִּיּוֹת. That reading echoes the conclusion that everyone's prayer is directed toward one place.

keyTerms.meaning: the verse's word read here through wordplay

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אָבִין, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי אֲבִינָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Avin said, and some say Rabbi Avina:
What verse points to this?
“Your neck is like the tower of David, built with turrets”—
a hill toward which all mouths turn.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אָבִין, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי אֲבִינָא: מַאי קְרָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It supplies a scriptural allusion to the conclusion that all direct themselves toward one place.
steps.raayaObject: The image of all mouths turning toward one place.

steps.title: Travelers pray before departure and recite קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע at its time
steps.stepSummary: אֲבוּהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל and לֵוִי prayed early before a journey, then recited קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע when its time arrived.
steps.simpleTranslation: When אֲבוּהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל and לֵוִי wanted to set out on a journey, they prayed early. When the time for קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע arrived, they recited it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns from prayer direction to the timing of prayer before travel. It reports what אֲבוּהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל and לֵוִי did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They prayed before setting out, but did not recite קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע until its time arrived. The next step will look for a teaching that fits this practice.

keyTerms.meaning: the sage who traveled with אֲבוּהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל
to set out on a journey

phrases.english: Shmuel's father and Levi,
when they wanted to set out on a journey,
would pray early,

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי הֲוָה מָטֵי זְמַן קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע קָרוּ.
phrases.english: and when the time for reciting Shema arrived, they recited it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The discussion leaves the shared direction of prayer and begins a case about travel and timing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Their practice was to pray before departure and wait until its time to recite קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע.

steps.title: An earlier teaching fits the travelers’ practice
steps.stepSummary: A teaching about early departure distinguishes acts done before leaving from קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע, which is recited when its time arrives.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view matches their practice? This תנא's: someone leaving early can sound a שׁוֹפָר, wave a לוּלָב, or read the מְגִילָּה as appropriate, and recites קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע when its time arrives. Someone leaving early by wagon or boat prays, and recites קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע when its time arrives.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whose teaching fits the travelers’ practice, then quotes one. The wagon-or-boat case states the match directly: pray before travel, and recite קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע when its time arrives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first case also repeats the rule to wait for the time of קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע. The second case adds the early prayer that matches the practice just reported.

keyTerms.meaning: a palm branch used for the ritual

steps.whatToRemember: In the quoted travel case, prayer comes before departure; קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע waits until its time.

phrases.english: According to whom? According to this teacher, as it was taught:
If someone rose early to set out on the road,
they bring him a shofar, and he sounds it,
a lulav, and he waves it,
a scroll, and he reads it,
and when the time for reciting Shema arrives, he recites it.
If he rose early to sit in a wagon or on a boat—

phrases.aramaic: מִתְפַּלֵּל, וּכְשֶׁיַּגִּיעַ זְמַן קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע — קוֹרֵא.
phrases.english: he prays, and when the time for reciting Shema arrives, he recites it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It identifies a teaching whose wagon-or-boat case follows the same prayer-then-קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע sequence.
steps.raayaObject: The travel practice of אֲבוּהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל and לֵוִי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The quoted teaching beginning הִשְׁכִּים לָצֵאת לַדֶּרֶךְ, especially its wagon-or-boat case.

steps.title: Keep redemption and prayer together
steps.stepSummary: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר favors saying קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע and then praying, even under the travel conditions already discussed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר says: In either case, recite קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע and pray, so that גְּאוּלָּה is joined to תְּפִלָּה.
steps.whatsHappening: A second view is added to the earlier travel case. It puts keeping גְּאוּלָּה and תְּפִלָּה together first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words “in either case” refer back to the travel situations already under discussion. This view prefers the order of קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע followed by prayer, even when travel affects how one can pray.

keyTerms.meaning: join the blessing of redemption directly to prayer

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
In either case,
one recites Shema and prays,
so that one joins redemption to prayer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the dissenting view within the same ברייתא; the practice of אֲבוּהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל and לֵוִי follows the first תנא, not this view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Keep גְּאוּלָּה next to תְּפִלָּה by reciting קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע and then praying.

steps.title: Identify the point of disagreement
steps.stepSummary: The גְּמָרָא asks what the two views value differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: What do they disagree about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גְּמָרָא pauses to ask what is behind the disagreement. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both views concern prayer during early travel. The question asks which benefit each view gives priority to.

phrases.english: What do they disagree about?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the competing views.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which consideration does each view consider more important?

steps.title: Standing versus keeping the prayers together
steps.stepSummary: One view prefers standing for תְּפִלָּה; the other prefers joining גְּאוּלָּה to תְּפִלָּה.
steps.simpleTranslation: One sage holds that standing for prayer is preferable, while the other holds that joining redemption to prayer is preferable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גְּמָרָא answers by naming the two priorities. It does not introduce a new travel case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Praying earlier can make it possible to stand. Praying after קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע keeps גְּאוּלָּה next to תְּפִלָּה; the views differ over which benefit should win here.

phrases.english: One sage holds that standing for prayer is preferable,

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר מִסְמָךְ גְּאוּלָּה לִתְפִלָּה עָדִיף.
phrases.english: and the other holds that joining redemption to prayer is preferable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by identifying the competing priorities.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The disagreement is whether standing for תְּפִלָּה or joining גְּאוּלָּה to תְּפִלָּה takes priority in this situation.
steps.whatToRemember: The dispute is about which prayer benefit takes priority during travel.

steps.title: A group prays before the lecture
steps.stepSummary: מָרִימָר and מָר זוּטְרָא gathered ten people to pray, then went to the festival lecture.
steps.simpleTranslation: מָרִימָר and מָר זוּטְרָא would gather ten people on the שַׁבָּת of the רֶגֶל and pray; afterward they would go out to the lecture.
steps.whatsHappening: The גְּמָרָא moves from the travel dispute to an example of arranging prayer around another obligation. This practice becomes an option suggested to רַב אָשֵׁי below.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They prayed with a group before leaving for the lecture. The passage reports what they did; it has not yet said that everyone must use this arrangement.

keyTerms.meaning: one of the sages in this account
the other sage in this account

phrases.english: Mareimar and Mar Zutra
would gather a group of ten
on the Shabbat of the festival and pray,
and afterward go out to the lecture.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָרִימָר וּמָר זוּטְרָא הֲווֹ מְכַנְּפִי בֵּי עַשְׂרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a related set of examples about prayer arrangements under time pressure.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Reports the practice of gathering ten to pray before going to the festival lecture.

steps.title: A different prayer arrangement
steps.stepSummary: רַב אָשֵׁי prayed seated alongside the congregation but individually, then prayed standing at home.
steps.simpleTranslation: רַב אָשֵׁי would pray individually, seated, at the same time as the congregation. When he came home, he would pray again while standing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גְּמָרָא gives a second example, this time from רַב אָשֵׁי. His arrangement differs from gathering ten people before the lecture.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His first prayer took place alongside the congregation, but the text calls it individual prayer. At home he prayed standing, so the account mentions both praying at the congregation’s time and standing.

keyTerms.meaning: the sage whose practice is described
at the same time as the congregation

phrases.english: Rav Ashi would pray
at the same time as the congregation, individually, while seated.
When he would come home,
he would pray again while standing.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי מְצַלֵּי בַּהֲדֵי צִבּוּרָא בְּיָחִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents another sage’s arrangement, which the following questions will test.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Reports that רַב אָשֵׁי prayed seated alongside the congregation and later prayed standing at home.
steps.confusionAlert: “Alongside the congregation” does not mean he joined their group prayer: the text explicitly says בְּיָחִיד, individually.

steps.title: Why not gather a group first?
steps.stepSummary: The sages ask why רַב אָשֵׁי does not follow the arrangement of מָרִימָר and מָר זוּטְרָא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The sages said to him: Let the Master do as מָרִימָר and מָר זוּטְרָא do!
steps.whatsHappening: The sages suggest the first arrangement as an alternative for רַב אָשֵׁי. Their question sets up his reason for not using it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מָרִימָר and מָר זוּטְרָא gathered ten and prayed before going to the lecture. The sages ask why רַב אָשֵׁי cannot do the same.

keyTerms.meaning: the Master; a respectful way to address him

phrases.english: The sages said to him:
Let the Master do as Mareimar and Mar Zutra do!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן: וְלַעֲבֵיד מָר כְּמָרִימָר וּמָר זוּטְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes the earlier practice as a simpler alternative to רַב אָשֵׁי’s practice.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does רַב אָשֵׁי not gather ten to pray before the lecture?

steps.title: Gathering the group is burdensome
steps.stepSummary: רַב אָשֵׁי says that the suggested arrangement is too burdensome for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: The matter is burdensome for me.
steps.whatsHappening: רַב אָשֵׁי answers the first suggestion. He gives a practical reason for not following that arrangement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His reply addresses gathering a group as מָרִימָר and מָר זוּטְרָא did. It does not yet address the different suggestion the sages raise next.

phrases.english: He said to them:
The matter is burdensome for me.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the first suggested arrangement on practical grounds.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Gathering a group in that way is too burdensome for רַב אָשֵׁי.

steps.title: Why not pray before leaving?
steps.stepSummary: The sages suggest following אֲבוּהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל and לֵוִי instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the Master do as אֲבוּהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל and לֵוִי do!
steps.whatsHappening: The sages now offer a second alternative. They point back to the earlier practice of אֲבוּהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל and לֵוִי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first suggestion involved gathering ten before the lecture. This question instead points to the earlier example of praying before departure.

keyTerms.meaning: the sage named alongside אֲבוּהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל

phrases.english: And let the Master do
as Shmuel’s father and Levi do!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different option after רַב אָשֵׁי declines to gather a group.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does רַב אָשֵׁי not follow the earlier practice of אֲבוּהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל and לֵוִי?

steps.title: He has not seen older sages do that
steps.stepSummary: רַב אָשֵׁי says he has not seen the older sages follow that practice.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: I have not seen sages older than us doing that.
steps.whatsHappening: רַב אָשֵׁי answers the second suggestion by appealing to the practice of older sages. This closes the exchange here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His first answer was about the burden of gathering a group. Here his reason is different: he has not seen older sages pray in the suggested way. The text reports his reason without stating a general prohibition.

phrases.english: He said to them:
I have not seen
sages older than us
who do it this way.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: לָא חֲזֵינָא לְהוּ לְרַבָּנַן קַשִּׁישֵׁי מִינַּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רַב אָשֵׁי does not adopt the second proposed practice.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רַב אָשֵׁי has not seen sages older than his group follow that practice.
steps.whatToRemember: רַב אָשֵׁי gives a separate answer to each suggestion: the group arrangement is burdensome, and the early-prayer arrangement is not one he has seen older sages follow.

steps.title: The משנה: Is מוסף only for a community?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says תפלת המוספין is said only with a חבר עיר. The חכמים say it is said both with and without a חבר עיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says: תפלת המוספין is only said with a חבר עיר. The חכמים say: It is said with a חבר עיר and without one.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It presents a disagreement about whether תפלת המוספין is only a communal prayer or also an obligation on every individual.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה sees מוסף as tied to the community, because it stands in place of the communal קרבן מוסף. The חכמים say it is an obligation on every person, whether or not he is part of a community group.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מַתְנִיתִין: 'our משנה.' A new משנה is starting.
The additional (מוסף) prayer said on שבת, יום טוב and ראש חודש
An organized community prayer group. The Sefaria translation calls it a quorum of ten.
The Sages. This is the majority opinion.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
phrases.notes: Marks the start of a new משנה

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya says:
The Mussaf prayer is not said
except with a community prayer group.
phrases.notes: So it is a communal prayer only.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
with a community prayer group, and without a community prayer group.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It follows the earlier discussion of how רב אשי and other אמוראים arranged their personal תפלה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה: מוסף is only with a חבר עיר. חכמים: it is said with or without a חבר עיר.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's version of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's view
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה quotes רבי אלעזר בן עזריה as saying that wherever there is a חבר עיר, the individual is exempt from מוסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says in his name: Any place where there is a חבר עיר, an individual is exempt from תפלת המוספין.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה gives a second version of what רבי אלעזר בן עזריה held. In his version, the existence of a community group is what frees the individual from saying מוסף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason for the exemption is that the שליח ציבור of the community covers the individual. So the exemption applies specifically where there is a חבר עיר.

keyTerms.meaning: In his name. Here it means in the name of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
An individual praying on his own

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה is not giving his own opinion here. He is reporting a different version of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's view.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says in his name:
phrases.notes: In the name of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ שָׁם חֶבֶר עִיר —
phrases.english: Any place where there is a community prayer group,
an individual is exempt from the Mussaf prayer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of the view of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה that was quoted in Step 32.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Where a חבר עיר exists, the individual is exempt from מוסף.

steps.title: Isn't רבי יהודה saying the same thing as the first version?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: רבי יהודה's version seems identical to the first version of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבי יהודה's view is the same as the תנא קמא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks why the משנה bothered to bring two versions. Both versions seem to say that an individual does not say מוסף when there is a community.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both versions link מוסף to the community. Neither one seems to require an individual to say it when a community exists. So the two versions look identical, and the second one seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for גְּמָרָא. The גמרא's discussion begins.
The first תנא. Here it means the first version of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's view.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Rabbi Yehuda's view is the same as the first tanna!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why the משנה needs the two versions in Steps 32 and 33.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for רבי יהודה's version of the view of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If both versions give the same outcome, the second version is repeating the first for no reason.

steps.title: The difference: an individual where there is no community group
steps.stepSummary: The two versions disagree about an individual living where there is no חבר עיר. In the first version he is exempt. In רבי יהודה's version he is obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them: a יחיד who is not in a place with a חבר עיר. The תנא קמא holds he is exempt, and רבי יהודה holds he is obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by finding a real case where the two versions give different rulings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, מוסף is purely a communal prayer, so an isolated individual never says it. In רבי יהודה's version, the individual is exempt only because the community's שליח ציבור covers him. With no community there, nobody covers him, so he must say מוסף himself.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them

steps.confusionAlert: 'שלא בחבר עיר' here means an individual in a place with no community group at all. It does not mean someone who simply did not attend the community's prayers.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them:
an individual who is not in a place with a community prayer group.
The first tanna holds he is exempt,
phrases.notes: Because מוסף is only a communal prayer

phrases.english: and Rabbi Yehuda holds he is obligated.
phrases.notes: Because no שליח ציבור is there to cover him

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 34.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a practical difference (נפקא מינה) between the two versions
steps.terutzMaskana: They differ about an individual where there is no חבר עיר: exempt in the first version, obligated in רבי יהודה's version.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's view. In the first, מוסף is purely communal. In רבי יהודה's version, the community exempts the individual, so an isolated individual must say מוסף himself.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה's version
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר חיננא, quoting רב חייא בר רב, rules that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה's version of the view of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר חיננא said in the name of רב חייא בר רב: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה, who spoke in the name of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא gives a practical ruling on the משנה's dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ruling chooses רבי יהודה's version. It does not follow the חכמים or the first version. So where a חבר עיר exists, the individual is exempt from מוסף, and where none exists, he is obligated.
steps.whyThisMatters: This turns the theoretical dispute into a practical ruling about when an individual must say מוסף.

phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Ḥinnana said
that Rav Ḥiyya bar Rav said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Yehuda,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה.
phrases.english: who spoke in the name of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בַּר חִינָּנָא אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר רַב הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the two versions are clearly distinguished in Step 35, this step rules on which one is the הלכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה's version of the view of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.

steps.title: Support from שמואל's personal practice
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בר אבין agrees with the ruling and supports it with שמואל's statement that he never said מוסף as an individual.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא בר אבין said to him: You have spoken well, as שמואל said: In all my days I never prayed מוסף as a יחיד...
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא backs up the ruling from Step 36 by pointing to the personal practice of שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On its own, 'I never prayed מוסף as an individual' could fit either version, since both say an individual is exempt where a community exists. The proof depends on how the statement ends. It continues on the next amud, where שמואל describes the one time he did pray alone: when no community prayer took place, so he was a יָחִיד שֶׁלֹּא בְּחֶבֶר עִיר. That is the case where רבי יהודה's version says the individual is obligated.

keyTerms.meaning: You have spoken well, you are correct

steps.confusionAlert: שמואל's statement is cut off here. Its continuation gives the exact setting, which is what ties it to רבי יהודה's version.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לֵיהּ רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין:
phrases.english: Rav Ḥiyya bar Avin said to him:
You have spoken well,
as Shmuel said:
In all my days I never prayed
the Mussaf prayer as an individual
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לֵיהּ רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין שַׁפִּיר קָאָמְרַתְּ דְּאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the ruling in Step 36.
steps.raayaObject: The ruling that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה's version of the view of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל's personal practice of never saying מוסף as an individual
